issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and the text before Lemma strangcireiglimitlm claim that c(T_n) is diagonalized by F_{p,n}, in contrast with general quaternion circulants. What the lemma actually proves is that the complex representation M(c(T_n)) is unitarily similar to a 2n-by-2n matrix that is block-diagonal with 2x2 blocks G[f_m](2pi s/n); this is exactly the block-diagonalization available for every quaternion circulant (cited from pan2024block). Writing c(T_n)=C_1+C_2 q with C_1,C_2 circulant over Q_(0,1), one gets F c(T_n) F^* = Lambda_1 + Lambda_2 J q with J the flip permutation, which is the X-shaped (non-diagonal) pattern the paper itself displays for general circulants; it is diagonal only when phi_2(f_m) vanishes at the grid points, which fails in both worked examples (phi_2(f) is not identically zero). Hence the advertised distinction between Strang's preconditioner and general circulants is unsupported and false in general.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the claim of diagonalization by the quaternion DFT and state instead that M(c(T_n)) is block-diagonalized with 2x2 blocks G[f_m](2pi s/n), as for general quaternion circulants; remove the claimed contrast with general circulants.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claim in the abstract/introduction and the sentence introducing Lemma strangcireiglimitlm are false; no formal theorem depends on it (the O(n log n) inversion cost and the spectral results only use block diagonalization).
issues.title: Strang preconditioner is not diagonalized by the quaternion DFT; only block-diagonalized like any quaternion circulant
issues.why_classification: An advertised distinguishing property of the preconditioner must be withdrawn outright (not merely weakened), although no formal result or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes that the Fourier coefficients of g:=conj(phi_1(f))-phi_1(f) vanish only for s>=0, then invokes density of trigonometric polynomials with indices s in {-l,...,l} to conclude g is orthogonal to all continuous functions. Vanishing of the nonnegative-index coefficients alone does not imply this (e.g. g=exp(-i x) has all nonnegative coefficients zero). The missing step is that g is purely imaginary, so conjugating gives vanishing of the negative-index coefficients too.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the observation that conj(g)=-g, so the s>=0 identities conjugated yield the s<0 identities, after which the density argument applies.
issues.overall_effect: Part (i) of the lemma is stated correctly but its proof has an unjustified inference; no downstream result is affected once the gap is closed.
issues.title: Density argument in Lemma gfuncstructurelm uses only nonnegative Fourier indices
issues.why_classification: A one-line local argument closes the gap and every claim survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: G[f](x) is defined with top-right entry -phi_2(f)(x) and bottom-left entry conj(phi_2(f)(x)); such a matrix is Hermitian only if phi_2(f)(x)=0, so the asserted Hermitian property is false and its eigenvalues are (a+d)/2 ± sqrt((a-d)^2-4|phi_2|^2)/2, generally non-real and not equal to the stated check f, hat f (which contain +4|phi_2|^2). The proof of (i) correctly derives the quadratic form with the Hermitian matrix having +phi_2(f)(x) in the top-right, and then asserts it equals G[f](x), which it does not. Parts (ii),(iii), Lemma strangcireiglimitlm and Appendix A all treat G[f] as Hermitian with eigenvalues check f, hat f.

failure_location.quote: It is clear that $G[f](x)$ is Hermitian for each $x$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace -phi_2(f)(x) by +phi_2(f)(x) in the definition of G[f](x) (and in the displayed G[f_m] blocks), which restores Hermiticity and consistency with the proof's own computation and with check f, hat f.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the identity in (i), the eigenvalue identifications lambda_min(G)=check f, lambda_max(G)=hat f, the block symbol in Appendix A, and the spectrum formula of Lemma strangcireiglimitlm refer to a non-Hermitian matrix; all are correct for the sign-corrected G.
issues.title: G[f](x) is defined with the wrong sign, is not Hermitian, and does not match the matrix derived in the proof
issues.why_classification: A single forced sign correction, dictated by the paper's own derivation, repairs the definition and all dependent statements without any loss.

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own definitions, for s'>=s the coefficient in \eqref{linearsys} is E(x(t-s') conj(x(t-s))) = E(x(tau) conj(x(tau-(s-s')))) with tau=t-s', a lag s-s'<=0, hence equal to conj(eta(s'-s)), not eta(s'-s). Thus the true normal-equation matrix is the conjugate (transpose) of the displayed T_n (e.g. for n=2 it is [[eta(0), eta(1)],[conj(eta(1)), eta(0)]]), and the system for the prediction coefficients should read T_n alpha = (eta(1),...,eta(n))^T with the displayed T_n, rather than T_n conj(alpha) = (conj eta(1),...)^T. The displayed T_n is still the Hermitian Toeplitz matrix generated by f in \eqref{genf}, so the later theory is unaffected, but the modeling claim that solving \eqref{hermqtsystem} yields the linear predictor is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the entry identification ([T_n]_{s',s}=conj(eta(s'-s)) for s'>s) or equivalently restate the system as T_n alpha = (eta(1),...,eta(n))^T with the displayed T_n.
issues.overall_effect: The link between the prediction problem \eqref{alphasoptimiz} and system \eqref{hermqtsystem} (unknown and right-hand side) is incorrect; the spectral and preconditioning results for T_n and the examples' generating functions remain valid.
issues.title: Normal equations for the quaternion linear predictor are identified with the wrong (conjugated) Toeplitz matrix
issues.why_classification: A local re-derivation of the indices fixes the modeling statement; the Hermitian Toeplitz structure, generating function, and all solver results survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $\sigma(\cdot)$ is right spectrum. Since $H_s$ is a Hermitian matrix, $\sigma(H_s)=\sigma(\bar{H}_s)$.

issues.failure_explanation: (a) Strang's preconditioner uses coefficients t_j with |j|<=floor((n-1)/2), so the eigenvalues of the circulant blocks are values of the partial sum f_{floor((n-1)/2)}, not f_{floor(n/2)}; for even n the statement (i) with m=floor(n/2) includes the extra terms t_{n/2}e^{i pi k}+conj(t_{n/2})e^{-i pi k}=(-1)^k 2Re(t_{n/2}) which are not present, so (i) is false as stated for even n (the index floor(n/2) is only correct for the range of the union). (b) In the simultaneous diagonalization by F, the s-th eigenvalue of c(conj(phi_1(T_n))) is conj(lambda_{n-s}(c(phi_1(T_n)))) = phi_1(f_m)(-2pi s/n), not conj(phi_1(f_m)(2pi s/n)) = phi_1(f_m)(2pi s/n); likewise the off-diagonal entries must be phi_2(f_m)(x_s) and conj(phi_2(f_m)(x_s)) up to a common sign. The displayed 2x2 blocks (with -phi_2, conj(phi_2) and equal real diagonal entries) are not Hermitian and have non-real eigenvalues phi_1 ± p|phi_2|, contradicting the realness of sigma(c(T_n)); consequently H_s is not Hermitian and the step sigma(H_s)=sigma(conj(H_s)) is unsupported, and the claimed permutation similarity G[f_m](-x)=P H_s P does not hold entrywise.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use m=floor((n-1)/2) for the partial sum (keeping floor(n/2) for the union range) and redo the block eigenvalue computation with correct index alignment, obtaining the Hermitian blocks [[phi_1(f_m)(x_s), phi_2(f_m)(x_s)],[conj(phi_2(f_m)(x_s)), phi_1(f_m)(-x_s)]] (up to a unitary sign change), whose eigenvalues are check f_m(x_s), hat f_m(x_s) and are even in x_s.
issues.overall_effect: Statement (i) is incorrect for even n as written and its proof is invalid; the corrected statement (with f_{floor((n-1)/2)} and Hermitian blocks having eigenvalues check f_m, hat f_m) and part (ii) hold, so Theorems strangcircprecedmatspectrumthm and strangcircmainthm are unaffected in substance.
issues.title: Eigenvalue bookkeeping for the blocks of M(c(T_n)) is wrong (partial-sum index and index alignment), invalidating the proof of Lemma strangcireiglimitlm(i)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a routine recomputation of the circulant block eigenvalues; the lemma's conclusions and all downstream results survive with only an index correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for some positive integers $p,q$ such that $p+q\leq 4n_0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The step replaces prod_{s=1}^{p} (1+eps-mu_s)/mu_s by prod_{s=1}^{4n_0} B with B=(1+eps-L)/L, L=2 check f_min/(3 hat f_max). Each factor is bounded by B since mu_s>=L, but extending the product from p to 4n_0 factors requires B>=1, i.e. L<=(1+eps)/2. Since L can be as large as 2/3 (check f_min close to hat f_max), B<1 is possible for small eps, in which case B^p > B^{4n_0} and the inequality, hence the stated constant C(eps), fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take C(eps):=2 max{1,B}^{4n_0} (or bound the product by max{1,B}^{p}<=max{1,B}^{4n_0}).
issues.overall_effect: The specific constant C(eps) is not justified for all admissible f and eps; the existence of some C(eps) and the rate eps^{k-4n_0} are unaffected.
issues.title: Product bound in the proof of Theorem strangcircmainthm assumes each factor is at least 1
issues.why_classification: A one-line adjustment of the constant fixes the argument with no change to the convergence guarantee.
